title: Policy-governed source escrow under an untrusted change proposal

runs.supports: Supporting assertions for §4 (fact visibility) and §5 (direct-attr classification), and the §3.3 wrapper decision. PREREG.md §4.2: fact visibility is a supporting assertion, not a primary claim -- an UNKNOWN fact constrains which selectors the matcher may rely on (§7.3), it does not refute C1-C4.
runs.expectedTrace: Each of owner/repo/rev/tag/githubBase/stripRoot/extension classified DERIVATION_ATTR, URL_FALLBACK or UNKNOWN, on BOTH Nix versions. escrow=true classified into exactly one of DIRECT_ATTR_REJECTED / DIRECT_ATTR_DROPPED / DIRECT_ATTR_SURVIVED, with DROPPED admissible only from a detector qualified by the sentinel on the same run.

nixValueVisibility.note: overrideAttrs preserved every probed public attribute at the Nix-value level on both versions: owner, repo, rev, tag, githubBase, stripRoot, extension, meta, name all present on BOTH the plain and the annotated source.

findings: The seven GitHub facts DO travel through derivation arguments on this pin, and the two Nix versions agree on all of them despite emitting different document schemas (envelope vs flat-map). The claim was measured, not read off the nixpkgs source.

tag is UNKNOWN in the derivation document because this fixture pins by rev and passes no tag. It is present=true at the Nix-VALUE level. That is a real difference between the two surfaces, not a contradiction, and it is why PREREG.md keeps §3.3 and §4 apart.
originHost has no direct attribute and is taken from the URL, recorded URL_FALLBACK. It is the only fact permitted to do so.

escrow = true is REJECTED at evaluation on both versions: nixpkgs' makeOverridable-wrapped fetchFromGitHub refuses the argument. The DROPPED branch was therefore never exercised, and remains an unmeasured outcome of this pin rather than an excluded one.
PREREG.md §3.3 comes back GREEN on both versions, so a wrapper is NOT justified and none is written. Writing one would be machinery invented for a failure nobody observed.
defectsFoundInThisRun: The probe recorded only the FIRST 1200 characters of an eval failure, which on a Nix error is the call-stack ladder and not the diagnosis. DIRECT_ATTR_REJECTED was therefore distinguishable from the other two outcomes while naming nothing about the rejection. Fixed in the next commit: head AND tail are recorded.

fixtureIdentity.chain: ann-{plain,marked}-{src,mid,top}: three derivations, so that 'direct consumer' and 'top-level' are not one derivation counted twice

runs.expectedTrace: source/consumer/top .drv DIFFERENT; source/consumer/top output SAME; NO REBUILD WORK; annotation visible to discovery YES; OBJECTS_REALISED count SAME, set DIFFERENT; realised-set sha256 DIFFERENT (registered expected churn, §3.5).
findings: C4 holds on BOTH Nix versions. Three .drv identities moved, three realised outputs did not, nothing was rebuilt, and the annotation is visible where a matcher would look.

The symmetric difference of the realised sets is exactly 3 objects leaving and 3 arriving, and EVERY one of the six is a .drv. That is the gap-23 arithmetic asserted rather than reconstructed afterwards: a non-.drv in that difference would be a moved output, which is C4 refuted.
The realised-set sha256 moved, as PREREG.md §3.5 registered in advance. It is expected churn. A later reading of that movement as a regression is a misreading of the pre-registration.

The visibility guard carries its red control in the report, not only in a test name: the unannotated source comes back false on the same reader in the same run. Without it, 'visible' is what the probe says about everything.
defectsFoundInThisRun: The shell-units job went RED on u26.1: the runner's shellcheck reported SC2015 (`A && B || C` is not if-then-else) on lib/pg-annotate.sh, where the locally installed shellcheck 0.11.0 was silent. The Nix measurement jobs were unaffected and their results stand. Fixed by replacing the construct with an explicit if -- the construct goes, not the finding. Recorded because it establishes that a lint mirror is only as good as the shellcheck version running it, and that the local mirror and the runner do NOT always agree.

runs.expectedTrace: A facts document with SEED_PROVENANCE=RECORDED; decisions carrying matched-rule provenance; SOURCE_ORIGIN_INDEPENDENCE PASS from a local ephemeral credential-free store with durablePromotion=false; a warm run agreeing with the cold one on every semantic field and differing only in elapsed time.

facts.note: A real graph, not a hand-written document. PREREG.md §11.1's condition for the corpus to count as evidence rather than as a mechanism test is now satisfiable.

decisions.note: Four rule/source pairs were INERT because originHost was UNKNOWN, and the report names which rule and which selector. PREREG.md §7.3 in practice: the rule did not match, and the reason is legible rather than mysterious.

findings: The facts document over the real fixture graph carries 150 dependencies and declares itself RECORDED. Every decision carries its matched rules and the trusted policy revision.

Four rule/source pairs were inert because originHost came back UNKNOWN, and the decision names the rule and the selector. That is PREREG.md §7.3 doing what it was written for: an UNKNOWN fact does not match, and the author of an inert rule can see why.
SOURCE_ORIGIN_INDEPENDENCE PASS from a store that was local, ephemeral and credential-free, with the guarantee named in the check.
CACH1 and CACH4 hold: cold 34.5s, warm 17.2s, a 2x speedup with every semantic field identical. The cache moved the clock and nothing else.
defectsFoundInThisRun: The CACH2 step used `find ... | head -1` under `set -o pipefail`, so find died of SIGPIPE and the step failed before looking at anything. That is the 'destroys its own specimen' shape listed BY NAME in this repository's own EXPERIMENT-PROTOCOL.md §1, reproduced verbatim in a step written by someone who had read it. Replaced with `find -print -quit`. CACH2 is therefore NOT MEASURED in this run.

p39.4 asserted a failure branch of nse_pg_scratch_prepare using a permission-based specimen that the function's own chmod defeats. The code was right and the test was wrong, twice. The branch that IS constructible is now tested; the branch that is not is described rather than faked.
notMeasured: CACH2 (a corrupted accelerator) -- the step died before it corrupted anything.
The ESCROW_REPLAY control (PREREG.md §16) -- the job failed at CACH2 before reaching it.

runs.supports: The §16 control (the strong guarantee still works with the policy machinery) and CACH2. The first run in which every job was green.
runs.expectedTrace: ESCROW_REPLAY PASS alongside SOURCE_ORIGIN_INDEPENDENCE PASS, proving the strong path is still compatible; and a corrupted accelerator object not becoming evidence.

cach2.observed: the run passed after an object in the shared staging store was corrupted

findings: PREREG.md §16 is satisfied: ESCROW_REPLAY PASS on the same fixture and the same machinery that produced SOURCE_ORIGIN_INDEPENDENCE PASS. The line has not quietly changed what the project proves by only ever exercising the cheaper guarantee.
Every job in this run was green. It is the first run for which that is true.
defectsFoundInThisRun: THE CACH2 STEP WAS NOT A SOUND MEASUREMENT, and its green is withdrawn rather than kept. Two defects. (1) It corrupted whichever store directory `find` returned first -- a zlib build output -- but under SOURCE_ORIGIN_INDEPENDENCE the escrow holds SOURCE material, so the corrupted object may not be in the population the guarantee covers at all. (2) It then read the resulting PASS as CACH2 holding, and a PASS cannot distinguish 'Nix rejected the corrupted bytes' from 'the corrupted bytes were copied into the escrow and replayed' -- which is the violation. A check that cannot emit its failing state is not a check (EXPERIMENT-PROTOCOL.md §1).

Rewritten for the next run: the victim is taken from the escrow's own discovery document so it is certainly a discovered source, and the verdict is decided by copying the object back OUT of the escrow into a fresh store and comparing hashes against the original and the corrupted content. VIOLATED, HELD_* and NOT_MEASURED_* are distinct outcomes, and NOT_MEASURED is recorded rather than rounded to a pass.
notMeasured: CACH2. Run 10's step produced a green that the step was not capable of earning, so it is recorded as INCONCLUSIVE and not as a pass.

runs.supports: CACH2, re-measured with a step capable of emitting its failing state; and PREREG.md §11.1 -- the SAME adversarial corpus, generated from a RECORDED facts document rather than a hand-written one.
runs.expectedTrace: CACH2 decided by copying the object back out of the escrow and comparing hashes, with VIOLATED, HELD_* and NOT_MEASURED_* as distinct outcomes. The corpus on a recorded seed: every control ACCEPTED, every head REJECTED.
findings: CACH2 HELD. A DISCOVERED SOURCE in the shared accelerator was corrupted -- one byte appended to hello-2.12.1/configure.ac, hash moved from 24814d9d to 88006ecf -- and the run REFUSED: exit 1, SOURCE_ORIGIN_INDEPENDENCE FAIL. The corrupted bytes did not reach the escrow, and the verdict was decided by an observation capable of saying VIOLATED rather than by reading a PASS as a hold.

This also explains run 4's inconclusive green: that step corrupted a zlib BUILD OUTPUT, which under SOURCE_ORIGIN_INDEPENDENCE is not in the population the escrow covers, so nothing it did could have been detected either way. A specimen outside the population is not a specimen, and the difference between the two runs is exactly that.

PREREG.md §11.1 is satisfied: the same five proposals, the same mutations, generated from a RECORDED facts document produced by a real Nix from a real graph. Every base-against-base control ACCEPTED and every head REJECTED at that scale. The corpus is no longer a mechanism test.
ESCROW_REPLAY PASS again (28.7s), so the §16 control holds on this commit too.
